worked_solution:
The tangential component of acceleration is given by

$$
{a}_{T}=\frac{v\cdot a}{||v||}.
$$

First, we compute the velocity vector by differentiating the position vector, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡4t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡4t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3t)⟩ \\  & =⟨-4\operatorname{sin}⁡4t,\,4\operatorname{cos}⁡4t,\,3⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute the acceleration vector by differentiating the velocity vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-4\operatorname{sin}⁡4t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4\operatorname{cos}⁡4t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3)⟩ \\  & =⟨-16\operatorname{cos}⁡4t,\,-16\operatorname{sin}⁡4t,\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we compute $v\cdot a$ and $||v||:$

$$
\begin{aligned}v\cdot a & =⟨-4\operatorname{sin}⁡4t,\,4\operatorname{cos}⁡4t,\,3⟩\cdot ⟨-16\operatorname{cos}⁡4t,\,-16\operatorname{sin}⁡4t,\,0⟩ \\  & =64\operatorname{sin}⁡4t\operatorname{cos}⁡4t-64\operatorname{cos}⁡4t\operatorname{sin}⁡4t \\  & =0 \\ ||v|| & =\sqrt{{(-4\operatorname{sin}⁡4t)}^{2}+{(4\operatorname{cos}⁡4t)}^{2}+{(3)}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{16{sin}^{2}⁡4t+16{cos}^{2}⁡4t+9} \\  & =\sqrt{16({sin}^{2}⁡4t+{cos}^{2}⁡4t)+9} \\  & =\sqrt{16+9} \\  & =\sqrt{25} \\  & =5\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the tangential component of the acceleration, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{T} & =\frac{v\cdot a}{||v||} \\  & =\frac{0}{5} \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$
